SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.claim: A verbal noun can follow a different verb pattern when the meanings match: أنبتكم نباتا is justified because أنبته is equivalent to قد نبت.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.claim: The same equivalence licenses اجتوروا تجاورا and تجاوروا اجتوارا, as well as انكسر كسرا and كسر انكسارا.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.anchor: وذلك قولك اجتوروا تجاورا وتجاوروا اجتوارا لأن معنى اجتوروا وتجاوروا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.speaker: ابن مسعود
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.claim: A reading attributed to Ibn Masعود has وأنزل الملائكة تنزيلا, since أنزل and نزل share a meaning.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءالمصدرفيهعلىغيرالفع.claim: Al-Qatami’s تتبعه اتباعا and Ruʾba’s تطويت انطواء show paired verbs with equivalent meanings; يدعه تركا is similar because يدع and يترك mean the same.

NAHHAS:v5p39/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p39/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p39/r3.claim: The verbal noun of أنبت is إنبات; the construction is paraphrased as “He caused you to grow as a plant.”
NAHHAS:v5p39/r3.anchor: ومصدر أنبت إنبات إلا أن التقدير فنبتهم نباتا

NAHHAS:v5p39/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p39/r4.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v5p39/r4.claim: One explanation connects the verse to Adam's creation from clay.
NAHHAS:v5p39/r4.anchor: قيل هذا لأن آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم خلق من طين

NAHHAS:v5p39/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p39/r5.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v5p39/r5.claim: Another explanation says the sperm drop is created from earth.

SAMIN-DURR:71:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:71:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:71:17/r1.claim: نباتا can be a verbal noun from أنبت with its extra letters removed, a so-called اسم مصدر.
SAMIN-DURR:71:17/r1.anchor: على حذف الزوائد، ويسمى اسم/ مصدر

SAMIN-DURR:71:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:71:17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:71:17/r2.claim: Alternatively it is accusative under an implicit نبتم; al-Zamakhshari says أنبتكم contains this sense, and al-Samin identifies this with the omitted-growth analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:71:17/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " أو نصب ب " أنبتكم " لتضمنه معنى نبتم "

SAMIN-DURR:71:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:71:17/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:71:17/r3.claim: The verb of growing people from earth is a strong metaphor.

ZAJJAJ:v5p229/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p229/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p229/r8.claim: Nabātan is a cognate accusative by meaning: anbata means “made you grow”; inbātan is the regular verbal noun, while nabātan is more emphatic.
ZAJJAJ:v5p229/r8.anchor: و (نباتا) محمول في المصدر على المعنى، لأن معنى

ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r1.claim: The Meccan surah is devoted entirely to Noah's preaching to his erring people.
ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r1.anchor: DEVOTED in its entirety to Noah's preaching to his erring fellow-men

ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r2.claim: The story symbolically portrays every conscious believer's struggle against blind materialism and the resulting loss of spiritual values.
ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r2.anchor: symbolically every conscious believer's struggle against blind materialism and the resulting lack of all spiritual values

ASAD-NOTES:71:17/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:71:17/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:71:17/r1.claim: God caused humanity to grow from the earth in gradual growth.
ASAD-NOTES:71:17/r1.anchor: God has caused you to grow out of the earth in [gradual] growth

ASAD-NOTES:71:17#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:71:17#n10/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:71:17#n10/r1.claim: Asad says each human body develops from organic and inorganic substances also found in the earth, elaborating the successive stages in 71:14.
ASAD-NOTES:71:17#n10/r1.anchor: the evolution of the individual human body out of the same substances - both organic and inorganic

ASAD-NOTES:71:17#n10/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:71:17#n10/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:71:17#n10/r2.claim: The phrase also refers to human species evolution from primitive organisms through increasingly complex bodily, mental, and spiritual development.
ASAD-NOTES:71:17#n10/r2.anchor: the evolution of the human species, which, starting from the most primitive organisms living on earth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p496/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p496/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p496/r1.claim: Although the six verses could be read as part of Noah’s speech, Islahi prefers to see them as divine insertions; verse 21’s renewed ‘Noah said, My Lord’ marks the transition back to his prayer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p496/r1.anchor: it seems to me that these are insertions from the Almighty in order to complete Noah’s speech.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r5.claim: The passage turns from signs in the heavens to signs on earth, presenting humanity first as earth’s noblest creatures.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r5.anchor: attention is directed at the signs of the earth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r6.claim: God grew humans from earth, returns them to it at death, and will bring them out of it again.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r6.anchor: the Almighty has grown them from the earth and later, to the earth He returns them and then He will bring them forth from it one day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r7.claim: The Qur’an’s eloquence makes the claim itself a clear proof: as vegetation grows, dies, and returns to earth, people do likewise; God’s revival of dead vegetation demonstrates His ability to resurrect people at will.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r7.anchor: just as vegetation sprouts from the earth, the Almighty has grown man from it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r8.claim: The verbal nouns emphasize their respective verbs, but by different modes of emphasis that are difficult to render in translation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r8.anchor: are meant to emphasize their respective verbs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r9.claim: The verb can suggest growth with power and wisdom, ease, or elaboration; Islahi prefers elaborate creation joined with divine might and wisdom, supported by parallel verses and his discussion at 71:14.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r9.anchor: I have preferred the translation which reflects the elaborate manner in which man was created as well as the might and wisdom

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r6.claim: Inbāt is metaphorical for creation: Adam was created from earth and his descendants came from him, so all humans may be said to have been grown from it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r6.anchor: والإنبات استعارة في الإنشاء، أنشأ آدم من الأرض وصارت ذريته منه، فصح نسبتهم كلهم إلى أنهم أنبتوا منها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r7.claim: Nabātan is accusative as a verbal noun with the extra letters deleted, meaning inbātan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r7.anchor: وانتصاب نباتا بأنبتكم مصدرا على حذف الزائد، أي إنباتا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r8.claim: Another parsing supplies an omitted verb: fa-nabattum, “then you grew.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r8.anchor: أو على إضمار فعل، أي فنبتم نباتا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also says the phrase means “He grew you, and you grew,” or makes nabātan accusative because anbatakum contains the sense of nabattum.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: المعنى أنبتكم فنبتم، أو نصب بأنبتكم لتضمنه معنى نبتم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r10.claim: The author says he cannot understand al-Zamakhshari’s second grammatical explanation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r10.anchor: ولا أعقل معنى هذا الوجه الثاني الذي ذكره

ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r1.claim: God created you from the earth; plant growth is a metaphor for origination because it vividly shows coming into being from earth, an observable process.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r1.anchor: أي أنشأكم منها فاستعير الإنبات للإنشاء لكونه أدل على الحدوث والتكون من الأرض لكونه محسوسا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r2.claim: The metaphor is an explicit, transferred verbal metaphor; deniers of resurrection are treated as though they also denied origination.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r2.anchor: وهم وإن لم ينكروا الحدوث جعلوا بإنكار البعث كمن أنكره ففي الكلام استعارة مصرحة تبعية

ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r3.claim: Min is an originative preposition referring to the remote source of creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r3.anchor: ومن ابتدائية داخلة على المبدأ البعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r4.speaker: أبو حيان وجماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan and others parse nabātan as an emphatic verbal noun for anbattukum, with the extra letters removed from the underlying form.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r4.anchor: قال أبو حيان وجماعة مصدر مؤكد لأنبتكم بحذف الزوائد والأصل إنباتا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r5.claim: Another parse supplies an omitted verb: fa-nabattum nabātan, you therefore grew as a plant.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r5.anchor: أو نصب بإضمار فعل أي فنبتم نباتا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r6.claim: The Kashf argues that inbāt and nabāt differ only in whether the act is viewed from agent or recipient, so no extra verb is needed; if inbāt keeps its lexical sense, it already entails growth.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r6.anchor: وفي الكشف أن الإنبات والنبات من الفعل والإنفعال وهما واحد في الحقيقة والإختلاف بالنسبة إلى القيام بالفاعل والقابل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r7.claim: If anbata means the conventional preliminary planting of a seed, the implied growth signals God's power and swift decree, as in 7:160.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r7.anchor: إن حمل على المتعارف من إطلاقه على مقدمة الإنبات من إخفاء الحب في الأرض مثلا فالوجه الحمل على أن المراد أنبتكم فنبتم نباتا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r8.claim: A further analysis reconstructs an original pair, anbatakum inbātan fa-nabattum nabātan, then omits the verbal noun from the first clause and the verb from the second by ellipsis.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r8.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الأصل انبتكم من الأرض إنباتا فنبتم نباتا فحذف من الجملة الأولى المصدر ومن الثانية الفعل اكتفاء بما ذكر في الأخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r9.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r9.claim: Al-Qadi says the wording is abbreviated because its meaning is supplied by entailment.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r9.anchor: وقال القاضي اختصر اكتفاء بالدلالة الإلتزامية

ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r10.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r10.claim: Al-Khafaji objects that al-Qadi's account misses the rhetorical indication already described.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#3/r10.anchor: وفيه على ما قال الخفاجي الأشعار المذكورة فتأمل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r2.claim: The verse points to Adam's origin: God created him from earth, and people are his descendants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r2.anchor: أراد مبدأ خلق آدم خلقه من الأرض والناس ولده

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r3.claim: Nabātan is used in place of verbal noun inbātan.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r3.anchor: وقوله: "نباتا" اسم جعل في موضع المصدر أي إنباتا قال الخليل:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r4.speaker: الخليل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r4.claim: Al-Khalīl paraphrases this as God making you grow, so that you grew as growth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r4.anchor: قال الخليل: مجازه: أنبتكم فنبتم نباتا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r3.claim: Growing is a metaphor for originating humans from earth because it better conveys their coming into being and formation from it; the fuller construction is abridged by entailment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r3.anchor: فاستعير الإنبات للإنشاء لأنه أدل على الحدوث والتكون من الأرض

BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r4.claim: The implied fuller wording is 'He caused you to grow from earth, then you grew'; the verse compresses this by relying on entailment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r4.anchor: إنباتا فنبتم نباتا، فاختصره اكتفاء بالدلالة الالتزامية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r1.claim: The sūra's aim is to show God's complete power to destroy those warned and replace them with better people, and to bring about the Resurrection that they deny; Noah's story establishes the threat through his people's destruction for rejecting him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r1.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على تمام القدرة على ما أنذر به

BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r2.claim: The basmala describes God as wholly perfect in majesty and generosity, universally giving outward blessings as al-Raḥmān, and granting His obedient allies lasting blessing as al-Raḥīm.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r2.anchor: الذي له الكمال كله من الجلال والإكرام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r6.claim: After the heavens, Biqāʿī returns to human creation, the greatest created thing and clearest sign of God, now specifying its details while explicitly establishing resurrection through a plant-growth metaphor.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r6.anchor: أعاد الدلالة بخلق الإنسان لأنه أعظم المحدثات وأدلها على الله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r7.claim: God grew humans from earth by creating their father Adam; the plant image recalls Adam's earthly origin and humanity's formation from earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r7.anchor: أي بخلق أبيكم آدم عليه الصلاة والسلام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r8.claim: The earth also supplies human food; people grow through that nourishment from the same earth from which they were created.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r8.anchor: من الأرض التي خلقنا منها , وبذلك الغذاء نمونا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r9.claim: Nabātan is a verbal noun used where the verb would ordinarily appear; stripping the augmented form signals how easy this creative origination is for God despite its wondrous novelty.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r9.anchor: إشارة إلى هوانه عليه سبحانه وتعالى وسهولته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r10.claim: The wording uses iḥtibāk: anbatakum implies a deleted first verbal noun, while the explicit second noun implies a deleted second verb, yielding anbatakum inbātan fa-nabattum nabātan.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r10.anchor: دال على حذف فعله أولا , ليكون التقدير

DURR-FULL:v8p291/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p291/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p291/r7.claim: Adam was created from the soil of the whole earth.
DURR-FULL:v8p291/r7.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا} قال: خلق آدم من أديم الأرض كلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r1.claim: After the argument from the heavens, Noah turns to the earth and its striking cycle of death and burial, preceded by the creation of people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r1.anchor: أنشأ الاستدلال بخلق السماوات حضور الأرض في الخيال فأعقب نوح به دليله السابق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r2.claim: The passage teaches that humans are formed from earth's elements like plants and embeds the promise of life after death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r2.anchor: وأدمج في ذلك تعليمهم بأن الإنسان مخلوق من عناصر الأرض مثل النبات وإعلامهم بأن بعد الموت حياة أخرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r3.claim: أنبتكم means “created you,” likening human creation to plant growth; the resemblance is especially close because humans are made from earth's elements, as in 3:37 and the idiom “God planted you for good.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r3.anchor: وأطلق على معنى : أنشأكم ، فعل { أنبتكم } للمشابهة بين إنشاء الإنسان وإنبات النبات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r4.claim: An unnamed view takes the implied meaning as “He grew your ancestor,” namely Adam, created from dust in 3:59.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r4.anchor: وقيل التقدير : أنبت أصلكم ، أي آدم عليه السلام ، قال تعالى : { كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r5.claim: نباتا is a verbal noun from أنبت treated as an emphatic direct object, rather than the regular إنباتا.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r5.anchor: و { نباتا } : اسم من أنبت ، عومل معاملة المصدر فوقع مفعولا مطلقا ل { أنبتكم } للتوكيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r6.claim: The lighter, established نباتا is preferred over the heavier إنباتا as a mark of eloquence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r6.anchor: لأن نباتا أخف فلما تسنى الإتيان به لأنه مستعمل فصيح لم يعدل عنه إلى الثقيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r17.claim: Growing humanity from earth is a metaphor: Adam was taken from earth, and all people grew from him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r17.anchor: أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا استعارة من حيث أخذ آدم عليه السلام من الأرض ثم صار الجميع نباتا منه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r18.claim: Nabātan is a verbal noun formed from a different source than the finite verb; the implied wording is fa-nabattum nabātan.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r18.anchor: وقوله تعالى: نباتا مصدر جار على غير المصدر، التقدير فنبتم نباتا،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r1.claim: Humanity’s initial creation from the earth refers to Adam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r1.anchor: والله أنبتكم من الأرض يعني أن مبتدأ خلقكم من الأرض هو آدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r2.speaker: الخليل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r2.claim: Al-Khalil paraphrases the phrase as you grew as plants.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says nabātan is a verbal noun used according to the sense, since anbatakum means made you grow.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج نباتا محمول في المصدر على المعنى لأن معنى أنبتكم جعلكم تنبتون نباتا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba notes a verbal noun formed differently from its verb, comparing tabtīlan from tabattala and referring to 73:8.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r4.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة هذا مما جاء فيه المصدر على غير المصدر لأنه جاء في نبت ومثله وتبتل إليه تبتيلا المزمل 8

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r5.speaker: الشاعر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r5.claim: An unnamed poet uses ittibāʿan as a verbal noun associated with the verb ittabiʿta, illustrating nonmatching verbal-noun forms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r5.anchor: قال الشاعر وخير الأمر ما استقبلت من … ه وليس بأن تتبعه اتباعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r6.speaker: الشاعر الآخر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r6.claim: A second unnamed poet’s ʿiwādan illustrates the same kind of verbal-noun formation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r6.anchor: وقال الآخر وإن شئتم تعاودنا عوادا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba generalizes that verbal nouns can differ in form from their verbs because differently formed verbs may share one meaning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p371#4/r7.anchor: وإنما تجيء المصادر مخالفة الأفعال لأن الأفعال وإن اختلفت أبنيتها واحدة في المعنى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r1.claim: Nabātan here is a verbal noun, a particularly apt form for describing God making humanity grow from the earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r1.anchor: هذا اسم مصدر، والإتيان به هاهنا أحسن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r4.claim: Noah invokes God's creative power and greatness and His heavenly and earthly benefits: God provides, made the sky a structure and earth a resting place, and expanded provision.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r4.anchor: وكل هذا مما ينبههم به نوح، عليه السلام على قدرة الله وعظمته في خلق السموات والأرض، ونعمه عليهم فيما جعل لهم من المنافع السماوية والأرضية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r5.claim: Because God alone creates and provides without peer, equal, partner, spouse, child, minister, or adviser, He alone must be worshipped.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r5.anchor: فهو الذي يجب أن يعبد ويوحد ولا يشرك به أحد؛ لأنه لا نظير له ولا عديل (3) له، ولا ند ولا كفء

JISHUMI:v10p7097/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7097/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7097/r11.claim: إنبات is bringing a plant out of the earth through gradual growth, stage by stage.
JISHUMI:v10p7097/r11.anchor: والإنبات: إخراج النبات من الأرض بالنمو حالا بعد حال

JISHUMI:v10p7097/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7097/r13.speaker: الخليل
JISHUMI:v10p7097/r13.claim: Al-Khalil parses نباتا as a verbal noun with a form unlike its verb's usual مصدر إنباتا, estimating أنبتكم فنبتم نباتا.
JISHUMI:v10p7097/r13.anchor: قال الخليل: تقديره أنبتكم، فنبتم نباتا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r22.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r22.claim: Ibn Jurayj says this refers to Adam, created from the soil of the whole earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r22.anchor: يعني آدم خلقه من أديم الأرض كلها , قاله ابن جريج

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r23.speaker: خالد بن معدان
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r23.claim: Khalid ibn Maʿdan says the human was created from clay and remarks that hearts soften in winter.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r23.anchor: وقال خالد بن معدان : خلق الإنسان من طين , فإنما تلين القلوب في الشتاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r24.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r24.claim: Ibn Baḥr takes the growth to describe development from smallness to largeness and from shortness to height.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r24.anchor: أنبتهم من الأرض بالكبر بعد الصغر , وبالطول بعد القصر , قاله ابن بحر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r25.claim: Al-Mawardi also allows that all creatures originate by nourishment from the earth's growth and substances.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r25.anchor: أن جميع الخلق أنشأهم باغتذاء ما تنبته الأرض وبما فيها , وهو محتمل

BURSEVI:v10p137/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p137/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p137/r6.claim: Humanity was wondrously brought from earth, either through the creation of their father Adam from it or through the chain of sperm, plants, and earthly food.
BURSEVI:v10p137/r6.anchor: وأنشأكم منها إنشاء غريبا بواسطة إنشاء أبيكم آدم منها أو أنش الكل منها من حيث إنه خلقهم من النطف

BURSEVI:v10p137/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p137/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p137/r7.claim: Nabātan is an emphatic verbal noun or noun of action in place of inbātan, confirming anbatakum; the following ikh r ājan likewise supports this construction.
BURSEVI:v10p137/r7.anchor: استعير الإنبات للإنشاء لكونه أدل على الحدوث والتكون من لأرض

BURSEVI:v10p137/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p137/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p137/r8.claim: Another analysis takes nabātan as a circumstantial accusative, indicating that humans are plantlike in earthly origin and growth, though they have an additional quality.
BURSEVI:v10p137/r8.anchor: نباتا حال لا مصدر ونبه بذلك إن الإنسان من وجه نبات من حي

BURSEVI:v10p137/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p137/r9.speaker: أهل المعرفة
BURSEVI:v10p137/r9.claim: People of spiritual knowledge read the verse as saying that bodily nourishment and growth come from the earth, as plants grow through water and soil.
BURSEVI:v10p137/r9.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعرفة والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا أي جعل غذاءكم الذي تنمو به أجسادكم من الأرض

MUQATIL:71:15-20/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:71:15-20/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:71:15-20/r4.claim: People's first creation was from earth's soil; nabatan means creation.
MUQATIL:71:15-20/r4.anchor: { والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا } [آية: 17] أول خلقكم من تراب الأرض، نباتا يعني خلقا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p284/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p284/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p284/r1.claim: God brought people into existence from earth, using the metaphor of a plant's growth; thus they grew like plants.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p284/r1.anchor: أنشاكم استعير الانبات للانشاء ﴿ نباتا ﴾ فنبتم نباتا

QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Adam was created from the soil of the whole earth; Qurtubi refers to his earlier discussion in al-Anʿam and al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r1.anchor: يعني آدم عليه السلام خلقه من أديم الأرض كلها، قاله ابن جريج

QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r2.speaker: خالد بن معدان
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r2.claim: Khalid ibn Maʿdan says humans were created from clay and that hearts therefore soften in winter.
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r2.anchor: وقال خالد بن معدان: خلق الإنسان من طين، فإنما تلين القلوب في الشتاء

QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r3.claim: Nabatan is a noun placed where the verbal noun would be: the verbal noun of anbata is inbat.
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r3.anchor: و«نباتا» مصدر على غير المصدر، لأن مصدره أنبت إنباتا

QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r4.speaker: الخليل، الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r4.claim: Al-Khalil and al-Zajjaj treat nabatan as a verbal noun based on the meaning: God made people grow with a growing.
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو مصدر محمول على المعنى، لأن معنى: «أنبتكم» جعلكم تنبتون نباتا، قاله الخليل والزجاج

QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r5.claim: Another reading of the syntax is 'He grew plants for you from the earth,' making nabatan an explicit cognate accusative; Qurtubi says the first analysis is clearer.
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r5.anchor: فـ«نباتا» على هذا نصب على المصدر الصريح. والأول أظهر

QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj also explains that God caused human beings to grow on earth, increasing them from childhood to adulthood and from shortness to height.
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r6.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: أنبتهم في الأرض بالكبر بعد الصغر وبالطول بعد القصر

QASHANI:71:15-20/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:71:15-20/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:71:15-20/r4.claim: God’s growing people from the earth means their emergence from the earth of the body.

RAZI-FULL:v30p124/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p124/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p124/r1.claim: The growth of people from the earth, their return to it, and their emergence again form the third proof of God's oneness.
RAZI-FULL:v30p124/r1.anchor: الدليل الثالث : على التوحيد قوله تعالى :

RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r1.claim: The verse returns to proofs within human selves and explains the creation in stages: humans are made from earth, returned to it, then brought out again.
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r1.anchor: فإنه بين أنه تعالى خلقهم من الأرض ثم يردهم إليها ثم يخرجهم منها مرة أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r2.claim: One interpretation takes the address as referring to Adam, the ancestor whom God grew from the earth, as with Adam's creation from dust.
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r2.anchor: أي أنبت أباكم من الأرض كما قال

RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r3.claim: A second interpretation says God grew all people from earth indirectly: nutrients produce plants, plants produce food, and food produces semen.
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r3.anchor: أنه تعالى أنبت الكل من الأرض لأنه تعالى إنما يخلقنا من النطف

RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r4.claim: The wording is elliptical: God caused you to grow, and you then grew as a remarkable growth, rather than the expected verbal noun meaning an act of growing.

RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r5.claim: Calling the growth wondrous makes the proof perceptible: God's act itself is unseen and would require revelation to establish, while the complete, marvelous plant growth can be observed.
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r5.anchor: يمكن الاستدلال به على كمال قدرة الله تعالى

STUDYQURAN:71:10/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:71:10/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:71:10/r12.claim: Verse 16 may begin “and that He” with verses 17 and 19, continuing the rhetorical question begun in verse 15.
STUDYQURAN:71:10/r12.anchor: V. 16 could be read with “and that He” at the beginning with vv. 17 and 19, also beginning with “and that,”

STUDYQURAN:71:10/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:71:10/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:71:10/r13.anchor: Like plants can mean “as growing things.”

STUDYQURAN:71:10/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:71:10/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:71:10/r14.claim: The phrase alludes to humans being created from dust, as in the likeness of Adam and Jesus described in 3:59.
STUDYQURAN:71:10/r14.anchor: On the one hand, this alludes to the creation of human beings from dust, as in 3:59

STUDYQURAN:71:10/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:71:10/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:71:10/r15.claim: The diversity of growing things also points to all things emerging from God as one ontological Source, whose substance is within them.
STUDYQURAN:71:10/r15.anchor: it alludes to the manner in which all things are thought to emerge from a single source, God.

TABATABAI:71:14-17/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:71:14-17/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:71:14-17/r12.claim: The verse speaks literally: human bodies arise from specially combined earthly elements that nourish, grow, and reproduce, which is the reality of plant growth.
TABATABAI:71:14-17/r12.anchor: فالكلام مسوق سوق الحقيقة من غير تشبيه واستعارة

AKHFASH:v2p550/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p550/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p550/r4.claim: He treats نبات as a verbal noun for the action, while identifying الإنبات as the regular verbal noun; نبات conveys the same meaning.
AKHFASH:v2p550/r4.anchor: فجعل النبات" المصدر، والمصدر "الإنبات" لأن هذا يدل على المعنى

TABRISI:71:15-17/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:71:15-17/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
TABRISI:71:15-17/r2.claim: Abu Amr reads mimma khatayahum with yāʾ; the other readers have khatiʾatihim with tāʾ, lengthening, and hamza.
TABRISI:71:15-17/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو مما خطاياهم والباقون مما خطيئاتهم بالتاء والمد والهمزة

TABRISI:71:15-17/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:71:15-17/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:71:15-17/r3.claim: The commentary says it discussed the variant in waladuhu in Surat Maryam.
TABRISI:71:15-17/r3.anchor: وقد ذكرنا الاختلاف في ولده في سورة مريم ع

TABRISI:71:15-17/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:71:15-17/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:71:15-17/r13.claim: Nabatan is an accusative verbal noun from an omitted verb, anbatakum fanabattum; al-Zajjaj says it follows the sense, since anbatakum means made you grow.

TABRISI:71:15-17/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:71:15-17/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:71:15-17/r20.claim: Humanity's original creation began with Adam, who was made from earth, and all people descend from him.
TABRISI:71:15-17/r20.anchor: يعني مبتدأ خلق آدم وآدم خلق من الأرض والناس ولده

TABRISI:71:18-23/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:71:18-23/r1.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:71:18-23/r1.claim: Another explanation is that God originated everyone through nourishment from what the earth grows and what grows within it.
TABRISI:71:18-23/r1.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه أنشأ جميع الخلق باغتذاء ما تنبته الأرض ونما فيها

TABRISI:71:18-23/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:71:18-23/r2.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:71:18-23/r2.claim: A further explanation describes growth from smallness to old age and from shortness to height.
TABRISI:71:18-23/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنبتكم من الأرض بالكبر بعد الصغر وبالطول بعد القصر

TABRISI:71:18-23/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:71:18-23/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:71:18-23/r7.claim: These favors show that God alone deserves worship without association, knows people's interests, and wisely governs them; people should not answer His blessings with disbelief and denial.
TABRISI:71:18-23/r7.anchor: وإنما عدد سبحانه هذه الضروب من النعم امتنانا على خلقه وتنبيها لهم على استحقاقه للعبادة خالصة من كل شرك

THALABI:v10p44#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p44#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p44#2/r8.claim: Nabātan is used where the expected verbal noun would be inbātan; it is a verbal noun differing from its regular form.
THALABI:v10p44#2/r8.anchor: وكان حقه إنباتا ولكنه مصدر مخالف للصدر

THALABI:v10p44#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p44#2/r9.speaker: الخليل
THALABI:v10p44#2/r9.claim: Al-Khalīl paraphrases the phrase as ‘you grew from the earth, growing.’

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes this as the beginning of Adam’s creation from the earth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: مبتدأ خلق آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r2.claim: Adam was created from the earth, and people are his descendants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: لأن آدم خلق من الأرض، # والناس ولده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r3.claim: The phrase means the beginning of your creation from the earth’s dust.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني أول خلقكم من تراب (¬2) الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r4.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash says the noun nabātan stands in place of the verbal noun inbāt, conveying the same sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r4.anchor: قال الأخفش في قوله: (نباتا) جعل الاسم في موضع المصدر (¬4)، والمصدر: الإنبات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r5.claim: Abū Isḥāq treats nabātan as a semantic verbal noun: anbatakum means He made you grow; the wording about your growing is more emphatic.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p260/r5.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (نباتا) محمول على المصدر في المعنى؛ لأن معنى أنبتكم: جعلكم تنبتون نباتا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:71:15-18/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:71:15-18/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:71:15-18/r4.claim: God made humanity sprout from earth: He created Adam from earth and his living descendants from him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:71:15-18/r4.anchor: والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا } جعلكم تنبتون من الأرض نباتا، وذلك أنه خلق آدم من الأرض وأولاده [أحياء] منه.

ELMALILI:71:17-20/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r1.claim: Nabat and nabt can be a collective noun for anything growing from the earth, conventionally especially grass or fodder, or a verbal noun meaning sprouting and growing; anbata means to make grow or bring forth.
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r1.anchor: İsim olduğuna göre yerde biten, yani neş’et edip yetişen her şeye denir, sonra sâkı olmayanda belki hayvânâtın yediğinde örf olmuştur

ELMALILI:71:17-20/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r2.claim: Growth is the distinguishing feature of vegetation, manifested through nourishment and reproduction.
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r2.anchor: Nebâtın faslı, mümeyyiz[^1] vasfı nümüvdür ki uzviyetin tegaddî ve tenasül ile

ELMALILI:71:17-20/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r3.speaker: المفسرون
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r3.claim: Commentators take nabatan as a cognate accusative rather than a circumstantial accusative because it is originally a verbal noun and human life is not simply plant life.
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r3.anchor: müfessirîn burada أَنۢبَتَكُم hâl değil, masdar olarak mef‘ûl-i mutlak olduğunu beyan[^2]

ELMALILI:71:17-20/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r4.claim: One grammatical explanation treats nabatan directly as the cognate accusative of anbata, with the sense that God raised you by growing you from the earth.
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r4.anchor: Ancak bazıları doğrudan doğru أَنۢبَتَكُم’den mef‘ûl-i mutlak olmak için

ELMALILI:71:17-20/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r5.claim: Another explanation makes nabatan the resultative verbal noun of an implied triliteral verb: God caused you to grow, and you grew a growth.
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r5.anchor: neticesi olmak üzere sülâsî bâbından mukadder olan fiilin masdarı olmak dolayısıyla

ELMALILI:71:17-20/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r6.speaker: الرازي
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r6.claim: Al-Razi gives two senses: God first created humanity through Adam from soil, as in 3:59, or created all people from the earth through seed, food, and plants that ultimately come from earth.
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r6.anchor: Râzî der ki: “Bunda iki mesele vardır. Birincisi: Âyette iki vecih var: birisi, ‘sizi Arz’dan bitirdi’ demek

ELMALILI:71:17-20/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r7.claim: Elmalılı endorses the point that the unusual wording makes human growth directly observable, allowing it to serve as evidence of God’s perfect power rather than requiring reliance only on revelation.
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r7.anchor: İkincisi اَنـْبَتَكُمْ إنـْبَاتًا denilmek gerekken اَنـْبَتَكُمْ نـَبَاتًا buyurulmuştur ki

ELMALILI:71:17-20/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r8.claim: Even if nabatan is taken as a circumstantial phrase the nuance remains, but commentators prefer its basic verbal-noun sense as a cognate accusative, which is prior and stronger than the circumstantial construction.
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r8.anchor: kelimenin esasen masdar olması ve mef‘ûl-i mutlakın hâlden akdem ve daha kuvvetli bulunması hasebiyle müfessirîn hâlden ziyade esası gözetmişlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:71:17/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:71:17/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:71:17/r1.claim: One interpretation takes the image as pointing to humanity's forefather Adam being created from soil.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:71:17/r1.anchor: iki türlü yorumlanmıştır: a) İnsanlığın atası olan Hz. Âdem’in topraktan yaratılışına bir işarettir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:71:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:71:17/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:71:17/r2.claim: A second interpretation compares human creation and development to plants because human nourishment comes directly or indirectly from the soil.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:71:17/r2.anchor: b) Her bir insanın gelişmesi ve yaşaması için gerekli olan besinler doğrudan veya dolaylı olarak topraktan alındığı için insanların yaratılıp geliştirilmesi bitkilerin yerden bitirilmesine benzetilmiştir

BURHAN:v2p393/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p393/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p393/r1.claim: In ‘I planted them with a planting,’ نباتا is not the true verbal noun of أنبت; the proper مصدر is الإنبات, while نبات names the result, like الكلام and السلام beside التكليم and التسليم.
BURHAN:v2p393/r1.anchor: قلت لاجرم حيث لم يرد الحقيقة هنا لم يؤكده بالمصدر الحقيقي القياسي بل عدل به إلى غيره وذلك لان مصدر انبت الانبات والنبات اسمه لا هو

BURHAN:v2p393/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p393/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p393/r4.claim: The object of أسررت is omitted and understood as supplication, warning, and the like; source-like emphasis can coexist with this ellipsis because the source form is not always used for literal emphasis.
BURHAN:v2p393/r4.anchor: وأما قوله تعالى ﴿ ثم إني أعلنت لهم وأسررت لهم إسرارا ﴾ فمفعول اسررت محذوف أي الدعاء والانذار ونحوه

BURHAN:v2p393/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p393/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p393/r5.claim: Two explanations reconcile إسرارا with the omitted object: it supplies a rhyme rather than emphasis, or أسررت is treated as intransitive after its object is disregarded, like ‘he gives and withholds.’
BURHAN:v2p393/r5.anchor: فان قلت التأكيد ينافي الحذف فالجواب من وجهين أحدهما أن المصدر لم يؤت به هنا للتاكيد وان كان بصورته لان المعنى ليس على ذلك

BURHAN:v2p393/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p393/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p393/r6.claim: Emphasis may use a synonym rather than the verb’s own source: جهارا is a kind of الدعاء, ليا a kind of distortion, and perhaps بهتانا a kind of wrongdoing.
BURHAN:v2p393/r6.anchor: ثم التأكيد بالمصدر تارة يجيء من لفظ الفعل كما سبق وتارة يجئ من مرادفه كقوله تعالى ﴿ إني دعوتهم جهارا ﴾

BURHAN:v2p397/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p397/r3.speaker: المبرد
BURHAN:v2p397/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad analyzes nabāt as governed by an omitted verb, meaning God made you grow from the earth and you grew; Ibn Khuruf chose this, Ibn Yaʿish agreed, and it was attributed to Sibawayh.
BURHAN:v2p397/r3.anchor: وهو قول المبرد واختاره ابن خروف

BURHAN:v2p397/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p397/r4.speaker: ابن عصفور
BURHAN:v2p397/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAsfur disputes the claim that the omitted-verb analysis is Sibawayh's position.
BURHAN:v2p397/r4.anchor: وزعم أنه مذهب سيبويه وكذا قال ابن يعيش ونازعه ابن عصفور

BURHAN:v2p397/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p397/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p397/r6.claim: Zarkashi distinguishes meanings: when the noun differs from the verb, an implied verb governs it, since a noncognate noun cannot emphasize or clarify that verb; when meanings match, the overt verb may govern it.
BURHAN:v2p397/r6.anchor: والرابع التفصيل بين أن يكون معنى الفعل غير معبر بمعنى مصدر ذلك الفعل الظاهر فهو منصوب بفعل مضمر يدل عليه ذلك الفعل الظاهر

ITQAN:v3p178/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p178/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p178/r6.claim: Emphasis may use a verbal noun from another verb or a concrete noun instead of a verbal noun: “vegetation” means “growing.”
ITQAN:v3p178/r6.anchor: وقد يؤكد بمصدر فعل آخر أو اسم عين نيابة عن المصدر

DAMGHANI:v1p447/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p447/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p447/r6.claim: Anbata can mean to create; God created humankind from the earth.
DAMGHANI:v1p447/r6.anchor: الثانى : النبات الخلق . قوله تعالى فى سورة نوح

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r4.claim: Nabāt can mean creation or origination from the earth.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r4.anchor: والثالث : الخلق . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة نوح

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r8.claim: The verbal noun nabāt is parsed as the object of an omitted verb: God made you grow, so you grew; likewise, He nurtured her and she grew.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r8.anchor: فالجواب ان المعنى : والله أنبتكم من الأرض فنبتم نباتا فيكون مصدر المحذوف مقدر
